title: Stabilize embed/rerank HTTP contract: cursor-scroll compatibility and deterministic error mapping
creator: Anika Patel
description: This ticket defines a migration and compatibility strategy to ensure a stable HTTP contract for embeddings and rerank endpoints across legacy clients and the new unified API. It covers three problem areas: pagination semantics (legacy page/limit vs. new opaque cursors), error-code alignment (consistent mapping for throttling, transient infra failures, and client errors), and token/cursor stability guarantees used by downstream search indexers and sync jobs.
background: Historically, older clients call /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank with page/limit and expect 200 shapes plus simple next_page integers. The new unified endpoints return opaque cursor tokens and richer structured responses. Several large customers reported breakage during early migrations: search indexers lost their position when cursors rotated, and clients misinterpreted 503 vs 429 leading to retry storms.
proposal: Introduce a compatibility layer that: 1) supports a legacy response shape when the request includes header 'X-RW-Compat: legacy=1' or query flag compat=legacy; 2) exposes 'rw_cursor' and a stable scroll token for long-lived access when clients opt in; 3) provides a deterministic HTTP error mapping table (see acceptance criteria) and sets Retry-After where appropriate; 4) offers a migration tool and backfill job for converting persisted page offsets to opaque cursors for major customers.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility header toggles legacy response shape and is documented in API reference
Cursor tokens returned for legacy mode are stable for at least 30 days and include a signed integrity HMAC
Error mapping implemented: map internal transient errors to 503 (server), throttle incidents to 429 with Retry-After, malformed requests 400, auth failures 401/403
Pagination semantics: legacy page+limit clients receive a numeric next_page when more results exist; unified clients continue to get opaque cursors
Integration tests that validate behavior across 5 representative client libraries (python/node/go/ruby/java) pass in CI
Monitoring dashboards and alerting thresholds for increased error-rate or elevated client retries are provisioned before canary rollout
tradeoffs: Maintaining dual shapes increases runtime complexity and test surface; mitigated with a short-lived feature-flag and strict deprecation window
Providing long-lived cursor stability restricts aggressive token rotation for security; we keep tokens HMAC-signed with 30-day TTL and optional rotation via admin API
Mapping 503->429 in some scenarios reduces client load but may hide legitimate infra outage signals from observability — we will only translate when underlying code sets a ThrottleKind flag
rollout_plan: Week 0: Implement middleware in runtime to emit legacy shapes behind feature flag; daily smoke tests
Week 1: Internal canary with Redwood platform-integrated services and SDK teams
Week 2: Beta canary for 3 large customers (opt-in), monitor retries and latency for 7 days
Week 3: Gradual ramp to all customers with logging of compat-header usage, then announce deprecation timeline for legacy clients (90 days)
test_plan: Unit tests for cursor encoding/decoding and HMAC validation
Contract tests verifying legacy response fields (items, next_page) vs. unified (items, cursor)
Chaos test: simulate transient infra errors and assert mapping to 429/503 follows policy
End-to-end migration test that backfills 5k persisted legacy offsets to cursors without data loss
monitoring_and_success_metrics: Rate of compat-header usage (target: <10% after 90-day deprecation)
Client retry rate within 5 minutes post-error (should decrease by >30% after mapping changes)
Number of customer-reported breakages related to pagination (target=0 during beta)
Average P50/P95 latency delta introduced by compatibility middleware (<2ms)
Number of long-lived cursor validation failures (target=0)

notes: Design decision: prefer explicit opt-in (compat header) instead of automatic content negotiation to avoid accidental mass rollouts
All mapped error responses MUST include 'x-rw-compat-error' header with internal code for debugging
Provide client migration guide with code snippets for converting page+offset loops to cursor-driven polling
